title: the congregation
hookLine: the congregation; why Sikhs never practice alone for long
last: EARN IT CLEAN, SHARE IT FIRST, KEEP THE NAME.

cards: Around certain people, a person gets funnier, kinder, braver. Around others, more anxious and quicker to gossip. Nobody gives an order; the room just does it.
It's why parents want to meet their kids' friends. People become, a little at a time, like the people they sit with. The Gurus built that plain fact into the center of Sikh life.

teach.b: Sangat. The congregation, the company you keep. You'll often hear sadh sangat, the company of the holy.
Everywhere Guru Nanak traveled, the stories say, he left a sangat behind: a small circle of people who met to sing the hymns, share food and look after one another.
Long before there were grand buildings, there were these circles of ordinary people. So what makes a sangat true?

teach.h: WHERE THE ONE NAME IS SPOKEN.
teach.b: The scripture asks that very question, and the answer, in paraphrase, is simple: where the one name is spoken. Not where the building is finest or the people richest.

Sikhs speak of the sangat with a startling kind of respect. There's a long tradition that the Guru is present wherever the sangat gathers, and that the congregation, deciding together, carries real weight.
That's why so much of Sikh life happens with others. Not because time alone is bad; remembering on your own breath matters.
But a person alone tends to drift, and a person in good company gets carried, the way a small boat is carried by a current.

how: Sikhs gather as a sangat in the gurdwara to sing kirtan, listen to the scripture, pray Ardas and eat langar together; many also meet in homes for readings and hymn-singing.

games.q: you're traveling from town to town teaching. what do you leave behind when you move on?
o: a small circle of people who meet to sing and share food.
nothing. the teaching goes with you.
games.why: the stories say Nanak left a sangat wherever he went: a circle that kept the hymns and the kitchen going.

practice: Bring to mind the people you spend the most time with. Not to judge them; just notice. Who do you leave feeling lighter?
Who helps you remember what matters? Picture one of them clearly, and let yourself be grateful for them, and stay there a while.

orig.note: Punjabi, in Gurmukhi script: the congregation, the company gathered together.

carryVoice: Your line: good company. You can't choose every room you're in, but you can choose some of them. Day fifteen.
